newsitem.title: USA: Indiana budget impasse has stalled new arena plans.
newsitem.headline: Indiana budget impasse has stalled new arena plans.

text.p: The Indiana state budget stalemate this week has also stalled financing plans for a new Indiana Pacers basketball arena, a spokeswoman for Indianapolis Mayor Stephen Goldsmith said Thursday.

Indianapolis officials still hope to gain passage of their proposals to partly fund the estimated $175 million cost for an arena when legislators meet for an upcoming special session on the budget, Gail Brown said.

One proposal to create a professional sports development district in downtown Indianapolis would harness approximately $5 million in existing sales and income tax revenues to back $50 million of bonds for a new arena, Brown said.

Indianapolis officials also seek up to $25 million from the state for infrastructure improvements for an arena, Brown said. That proposal had been pared to $4.7 million by the end of the session on Tuesday night, she said.
"We have a timing issue, if this arena goes forward we are trying to get it open by the 1999-2000 season, so we are pushed a bit," Brown said.
In the meantime, the city will continue planning for the arena right "up to digging dirt," Brown said.
"We have got to get some actual construction going soon," Brown said. "Sooner is better for us."
The Pacers have committed up to $2 million to keep the project on track while awaiting the completion of a financing plan, Brown said.

The professional sports district legislation had been approved by both houses of the Indiana legislature, amended in conference committee and passed by the state Senate, Brown said. Representatives held the legislation while considering the budget and did not pass the amended version, she said.
